step: Step 0: Pre-registration + Article XX Problem Existence Gate

q1_does_failure_occur.evidence: Over-drainage is a well-documented complication of CSF shunts. Symptoms include subdural hematoma (from low ICP), slit ventricle syndrome, and chronic headaches. Published rates: 10-20% of shunted patients experience some over-drainage. The eShunt drains CSF to the venous system at a fixed rate — nocturnal venous pressure rises (supine posture) interact with fixed drainage to cause positional over-drainage. This is established shunt physiology.

q2_does_it_matter_to_buyer.evidence: Over-drainage is the #2 complication of CSF shunts (after obstruction). It causes morbidity (headaches, hematomas) and may require shunt revision. CereVasc needs to demonstrate drainage safety for regulatory approval. An adaptive drainage controller that reduces over-drainage by ≥30% would be a major clinical differentiator vs fixed-rate VP shunts.

q3_does_mechanism_change_physical_quanti.evidence: M5_REFINED adjusts drainage rate based on venous pressure + sleep state. SC3 adjusts drainage rate based on ICP derivative (dICP/dt). Both act directly on the drainage rate variable that causes over-drainage.
q3_does_mechanism_change_physical_quanti.mechanism_acting_on_variable: Drainage rate is the physical quantity. Both controllers modulate it.

q4_is_change_large_enough.evidence: The pre-registered threshold is ≥30% over-drainage reduction vs fixed-rate drainage. V3 estimates M5 at ≥30% (nominal) but misses REM. SC3 estimated at ≥25% but covers REM. V4 must simulate both head-to-head.
q4_is_change_large_enough.uncertainty: The threshold is clinically meaningful (30% reduction in over-drainage symptoms). The question is whether either controller achieves it across ALL sleep stages including REM.

q5_does_intervention_create_larger_failu.answer: CONDITIONAL — adaptive controllers can UNDER-drain (causing hydrocephalus) or oscillate
q5_does_intervention_create_larger_failu.evidence: An adaptive controller that reduces drainage too aggressively can cause under-drainage → ICP elevation → hydrocephalus crisis. This is the DUAL risk of adaptive drainage. The controller must not over-correct.
q5_does_intervention_create_larger_failu.uncertainty: Need to simulate under-drainage risk as well as over-drainage reduction.

article_xx_problem_existence_gate.gate_verdict: PASS — problem exists (over-drainage is #2 shunt complication), matters to buyer (HIGH), mechanism acts on drainage rate. V4 must answer q4 (is the change large enough) and q5 (under-drainage risk) through simulation.

M5_REFINED.mechanism: Sleep-state venous-pressure-aware adaptive drainage. Uses ICP + venous pressure sensors. B-wave tolerant controller.
M5_REFINED.strength: Low false positive rate (B-wave tolerant), novel §103 position (venous pressure + sleep = novel combination)
M5_REFINED.critical_weakness: B-wave controller MISSES REM apnea (most severe sleep stage, 100% miss rate). REM apnea causes the most dangerous ICP spikes.

SC3_ICP_derivative.mechanism: ICP derivative controller. Uses ICP sensor only. Detects rapid ICP rise (dICP/dt threshold).
SC3_ICP_derivative.strength: Covers REM apnea (ICP rises in REM), simpler (1 sensor), lower cost, better patient transfer
SC3_ICP_derivative.weakness: Higher false positive rate (dICP/dt also triggers on cough), §103 risk (dICP/dt is known technique), estimated 25% over-drainage reduction (below 30% threshold)

v3_state_inherited.V3_verdict: PROVISIONAL_PARTIAL_V3 — M5 has critical REM weakness. SC3 does NOT dominate. V4 must run head-to-head simulation.

step_1_sc3_head_to_head_simulation.question: Does SC3 achieve ≥30% over-drainage reduction across ALL sleep stages (NREM, REM, mixed)?
step_1_sc3_head_to_head_simulation.what_would_kill_M5: If SC3 achieves ≥30% AND covers REM, M5's complexity (2 sensors, venous calibration) is not justified → pivot to SC3.
step_1_sc3_head_to_head_simulation.what_would_kill_SC3: If SC3 achieves <30% OR has excessive false positives (cough-triggered drainage reduction), SC3 is insufficient → M5+SC3 hybrid needed.

step_2_rem_apnea_attack.question: Can ANY controller cover REM apnea without excessive false positives?
step_2_rem_apnea_attack.physics: REM apnea causes ICP to rise rapidly (10-30 mmHg in 10-30 seconds). B-wave controller misses this because REM apnea is not a B-wave. dICP/dt controller catches it but also catches coughs (which cause similar rapid ICP rises). The question is whether the signal-to-noise ratio is sufficient.
step_2_rem_apnea_attack.what_would_kill_both: If REM apnea cannot be distinguished from cough/posture change by any controller, the adaptive drainage concept has a fundamental observability ceiling — similar to #1 V25.

step_3_hybrid_m5_sc3_assessment.question: Does a hybrid M5+SC3 controller (venous pressure for B-waves + dICP/dt for REM) achieve ≥30% without excessive false positives?
step_3_hybrid_m5_sc3_assessment.what_would_kill_hybrid: If the hybrid's complexity (2 sensors + derivative logic + calibration) introduces failure modes worse than the problem (sensor drift, calibration error, controller oscillation), the hybrid is not viable.

step_4_under_drainage_risk.question: Does the adaptive controller cause under-drainage (ICP elevation) when it reduces drainage?
step_4_under_drainage_risk.pre_registered_threshold: Under-drainage events (ICP > 25 mmHg for > 1 hour) must be < 5% of simulation time

step_5_identifiability_pre_check.question: Can the controller distinguish disease progression (real ICP change) from sensor drift / posture change / cough?
step_5_identifiability_pre_check.why_this_matters: #1 V25 lesson — if the system cannot distinguish real signal from noise, the controller will mis-tune. This is the #1 identifiability ceiling applied to #8.
step_5_identifiability_pre_check.what_would_kill_it: If ICP, venous pressure, and dICP/dt are collinear with sensor drift, the controller's parameter estimates are non-identifiable — same ceiling as #1.

pre_registered_thresholds.T2_rem_coverage: REM apnea events must be detected with ≥80% sensitivity
pre_registered_thresholds.T3_false_positive_rate: <10% false positive rate (drainage reduction triggered when no over-drainage risk)
pre_registered_thresholds.T4_under_drainage_risk: ICP > 25 mmHg for > 1 hour must occur < 5% of simulation time
pre_registered_thresholds.T5_identifiability: Controller parameters must be structurally identifiable (Jacobian rank check) — per #1 V25 lesson

what_would_constitute_gate_gaming: Simulating only NREM sleep (where M5 performs well) and excluding REM
Using a low cough/posture noise floor to make SC3's false positive rate look acceptable
Averaging over-drainage reduction across stages without reporting per-stage breakdown
Skipping the identifiability pre-check because 'the controller works in simulation'

honest_starting_position.M5_strength: Novel mechanism (venous pressure + sleep state), low false positives, good §103 position
honest_starting_position.M5_weakness: Misses REM apnea — the most dangerous sleep stage for ICP spikes
honest_starting_position.SC3_strength: Covers REM, simpler, lower cost, better transferability
honest_starting_position.SC3_weakness: False positives (cough), §103 risk (known technique), estimated below 30% threshold
honest_starting_position.most_likely_outcome: Neither M5 nor SC3 alone achieves ≥30% across ALL stages. Hybrid M5+SC3 may work but adds complexity. The identifiability pre-check (#1 V25 lesson) may reveal that REM apnea cannot be reliably distinguished from cough — which would be a negative ceiling for the entire adaptive drainage concept.
